title: Yara and the Autopsy Revisited
premise: Mara Hartwell has spent a decade as the cathedral archivist of Ashenmoor, cataloguing the town's secrets while keeping her own buried—including her sister Yara's disappearance ten years ago, officially closed after an autopsy she never believed. When a donated diary belonging to missing schoolteacher Elise Vann arrives with entries dated after Elise vanished, Mara realizes the crypt's locked ledger holds a coded record of who really died that winter—and why. As she decodes it, she finds Yara's handwriting woven through the pages: her sister never left Ashenmoor at all. The climax forces Mara to choose between exposing the town's beloved founder-descendants and protecting the only family she has left, ending with Mara opening the crypt publicly, Yara alive but complicit, and Mara choosing truth over belonging—then discovering belonging can survive it.
about_author: J. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent seven years transcribing centuries of births, deaths, and quiet scandals in rural England. Their fiction explores what small towns bury and what archivists refuse to forget.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Establishes her ordered world in the cathedral archive: every secret filed, every question deflected. She catalogs a donation box containing Elise Vann's diary and feels an old unease. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness, the comfort of systems over people.

chapters.title: An Entry After the End
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Reading Elise's diary for provenance, Mara finds an entry dated nine days after Elise disappeared. Her hands shake; she checks the accession record twice. Emotional beat: the first crack in ten years of certainty.

chapters.title: What the Constable Kept
chapters.summary: Mara visits retired constable Denny Foulkes, who closed both cases. He is evasive but lets slip that the original autopsy report was 'corrected' before filing. Emotional beat: dread dressed as politeness; Mara realizes the town protected someone.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the crypt registry—a ledger displayed openly behind glass—she notices columns of dates that don't match burials. Numbers repeat in patterns. Emotional beat: the thrill of recognition tangled with fear that someone wanted this found—or found by no one.

chapters.title: Yara's Hand
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, flashback-tinged. Comparing marginal annotations in the ledger to old letters, Mara confirms the handwriting is her sister's. Yara was alive in Ashenmoor after her disappearance. Emotional beat: grief inverted into hope, then into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Founder's Daughters
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She investigates the Calloway family, whose ancestors endowed the cathedral and whose matriarch, Vivian, funds the archive. A charity dinner scene where Vivian watches Mara too closely. Emotional beat: the seduction and menace of belonging.

chapters.title: Nine Days Missing
chapters.summary: Elise's diary POV via excerpts interleaved with Mara's reading. Elise documented the Calloway estate's financial fraud feeding the cathedral restoration. Her last confident entry: 'I have proof.' Emotional beat: mounting dread on two timelines.

chapters.title: A Question of Bones
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She obtains the sealed autopsy file through a favor from Dr. Imogen Reyes: the body identified as Elise Vann had the wrong dental records. It wasn't Elise. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the town buried a stranger and called it closure.

chapters.title: The Man Who Filed Lies
chapters.summary: Denny Foulkes' POV. His guilt-ridden interiority: he was paid to close the case, told the body was 'close enough.' He remembers a second figure at the quarry that night. Emotional beat: shame curdling into self-protection.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Archive materials are disturbed; her desk searched. A note in Yara's hand: STOP. Mara realizes her sister may be watching—or warning her. Emotional beat: paranoia where love used to be.

chapters.title: The Crypt Key
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She learns the crypt key rotates among three trustees: Vivian Calloway, the dean, and—until ten years ago—her own father. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing everything; her family was inside the circle all along.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Vespers
chapters.summary: Mara confronts Vivian after service. Vivian neither denies nor confesses; she offers Mara a funded fellowship abroad—an elegant bribe. Emotional beat: temptation offered in the language of kindness.

chapters.title: Decoding the Dead Columns
chapters.summary: Mara and Imogen work through the night cracking the ledger cipher: burial dates encode payments, and one column lists names of people paid to disappear—including a line item dated the week Yara vanished. Emotional beat: intellectual triumph shadowed by personal horror.

chapters.title: My Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara searches her late father's effects and finds his copy of the cipher key and unsent letters to Yara. He knew she lived; he helped hide her. Emotional beat: love and complicity indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Quarry at Night
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following the diary's clues, she goes to the flooded quarry where the body was found. Someone follows her; she escapes but drops the diary. Emotional beat: terror, and the loss of her only hard evidence.

chapters.title: Vivian's Version
chapters.summary: Vivian Calloway's POV. Her justification: Elise threatened the cathedral and three hundred jobs; the death was an accident covered up badly, then maintained deliberately. She claims Yara chose exile willingly. Emotional beat: chilling plausibility—the villain who believes herself the guardian.

chapters.title: Sister, Alive
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Yara finally appears—at their mother's grave. She admits she witnessed the cover-up and traded silence for protection, letting Mara believe her dead rather than make her complicit. Emotional beat: reunion laced with fury and relief.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Yara begs her to let it stand: exposure destroys the town, the cathedral, and Yara herself. Mara must decide between the sister she mourned and the truth she serves. Emotional beat: the book's thematic crux—loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: The Dean's Confession
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The dying dean, unwilling to be the last liar, gives Mara a sworn statement and the original autopsy draft naming who moved the body. Emotional beat: an unexpected ally; the machinery of truth begins turning.

chapters.title: Opening the Crypt
chapters.summary: Climax. At the founders' memorial service, Mara unlocks the crypt before the congregation and reads the decoded ledger aloud. Vivian moves to stop her; Denny Foulkes, choosing truth at last, corroborates. Emotional beat: public rupture, Mara's voice steady while everything breaks.

chapters.title: After the Reading
chapters.summary: Falling action, Mara's POV. Arrests begin; the town splits between gratitude and rage. Yara, facing charges for her silence, asks if Mara regrets it. Emotional beat: exhaustion, grief, and the strange lightness of having nothing hidden.

chapters.title: A New Index
chapters.summary: Resolution, Mara's POV. Months later, Mara rebuilds the archive honestly, misfiled nothing, hiding no one. Yara, sentenced to community service, works beside her re-cataloguing the crypt. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on truth rather than secrecy—quiet, earned peace.
